about: The complete documentation for the legacy tables built by build_legacy.py. context.py cuts it down to each readiness level. Every field is tagged by the kind of context it is: descriptions, structure, codes, units, rules, examples.

PSN_MST.description: Person master. People who have ever been employed.
PSN_MST.grain: One row per person, whether or not they are employed now.
rules: This table does not say who is employed now. Use ASG_HST for that.

codes.05: Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander

JB_REF.description: Job reference. The jobs a person can hold, grouped into job families.
JB_REF.grain: One row per job code. A job family has three or four job codes, one per level.
joins: JB_REF.PRED_FAM_CD = JB_REF.FAM_CD of the older family this family grew out of
rules: Family-level columns (FAM_DESC, AI_EXP_VAL, FAM_STRT_YR, PRED_FAM_CD, CRIT_FL) repeat on every job code in the family. Do not sum them across rows.
AI_EXP_VAL is an assumption set by the people who built the data. It is not a measurement.

LVL_NO.description: Level of the job within its family.
LVL_NO.units: 1 is the entry level. Higher is more senior.

SOC_CD.units: Standard Occupational Classification 2018, six digits with a hyphen.

AI_EXP_VAL.description: AI exposure value for the job family.

RNG_MIN.description: Bottom of the pay range for the job.
RNG_MIN.units: US dollars per year. Note that pay rates in ASG_HST and ACT_LOG are per month.

RNG_MAX.description: Top of the pay range for the job.

FAM_STRT_YR.description: Year the job family was introduced.

codes.NULL: The family existed before the first year of data

PRED_FAM_CD.description: Family code of the predecessor family.

codes.Y: The family is on the critical-roles list
This is the highest level in the family

ORG_REF.description: Organisation reference. The units of the organisation, as a hierarchy.
ORG_REF.grain: One row per organisational unit at any level of the hierarchy.
joins: ORG_REF.PAR_ORG_CD = ORG_REF.ORG_CD of the parent unit
rules: People are assigned only to units at level 4. To count people in a division or department, use ORG_PATH or walk PAR_ORG_CD upward. Matching ORG_CD to the division's own code finds nobody.

codes.Y: The unit has no units below it

ORG_PATH.units: The codes from level 1 down to this unit, joined by '/'. Example: C00000/C10000/C11000/C11100.

ASG_HST.description: Assignment history. The job, unit and pay rate each person has held over time.
ASG_HST.grain: One row per person per period in which job, unit, position and pay rate all stayed the same. A pay rise starts a new row, so one job spans many rows.
rules: Leave out rows where VOID_FL = 'Y' in every count and every pay figure. They were entered in error and are kept only for audit.
Some void rows are flagged current for people who have already left, so CUR_FL = 'Y' alone overcounts.
A person is employed on the extract date if they have a row with CUR_FL = 'Y' and VOID_FL = 'N'. Count people with count(distinct PSN_NO).
For headcount on a past date D, use EFF_DT <= D and END_DT >= D and VOID_FL = 'N'.
After a person leaves, their last row keeps the leaving date as END_DT. There are no rows for time not employed.

codes.9999-12-31: The row is still open. This column is never NULL

BASE_RT.units: US dollars per month. Multiply by 12 for annual salary.

ACT_CD.description: Code of the personnel action that started the row.

codes.C45: Career move into a different job family

codes.Y: The row is the open one for that person
The row was entered in error

ACT_LOG.description: Action log. Personnel actions such as hires, pay changes, moves and departures.
ACT_LOG.grain: One row per personnel action for one person on one date.
rules: This table has no void rows. Every row counts.
Each person has exactly one H10 row.
A departure is any of the five codes T61 to T65. For a departure, NEW_RT repeats PRV_RT.
For a new hire, PRV_RT is NULL.

codes.C45: Career move into a different job family

PRV_RT.description: Rate of pay before the action.

NEW_RT.description: Rate of pay after the action.

LV_HST.description: Leave history. Periods of leave taken by a person.
LV_HST.grain: One row per period of leave.
rules: Leave does not end an assignment. A person on leave still has their ASG_HST row.

metrics: Headcount: count(distinct PSN_NO) from ASG_HST where CUR_FL = 'Y' and VOID_FL = 'N'.
Annual salary: BASE_RT * 12 on a valid row.
Age on a date: whole years between BRTH_DT and that date.
Departures: ACT_LOG rows with ACT_CD in ('T61','T62','T63','T64','T65').

examples.question: How many people are employed in each career track now?
examples.sql: select j.TRK_CD, count(distinct a.PSN_NO) from ASG_HST a join JB_REF j on j.JB_CD = a.JB_CD where a.CUR_FL = 'Y' and a.VOID_FL = 'N' group by j.TRK_CD

examples.question: What is the average annual salary of people now in level 3 jobs?
examples.sql: select round(avg(a.BASE_RT * 12)) from ASG_HST a join JB_REF j on j.JB_CD = a.JB_CD where a.CUR_FL = 'Y' and a.VOID_FL = 'N' and j.LVL_NO = 3

examples.question: How many involuntary terminations were there in 2019?
examples.sql: select count(*) from ACT_LOG where ACT_CD = 'T63' and ACT_DT between date '2019-01-01' and date '2019-12-31'

examples.question: How many people were employed in the Insurance Operations division on 31 December 2015?
examples.sql: select count(distinct a.PSN_NO) from ASG_HST a join ORG_REF o on o.ORG_CD = a.ORG_CD where a.VOID_FL = 'N' and a.EFF_DT <= date '2015-12-31' and a.END_DT >= date '2015-12-31' and o.ORG_PATH like '%/' || (select ORG_CD from ORG_REF where ORG_TTL = 'Insurance Operations' and ORG_LVL = 2) || '/%'

examples.question: How many people employed now are under 30 on the extract date?
examples.sql: select count(distinct a.PSN_NO) from ASG_HST a join PSN_MST p on p.PSN_NO = a.PSN_NO where a.CUR_FL = 'Y' and a.VOID_FL = 'N' and p.BRTH_DT > date '2026-10-31' - interval 30 year

examples.question: How many men have ever been employed?
examples.sql: select count(*) from PSN_MST where GNDR_CD = '1'

misleading.about: Wrong documentation, used only by the 'misleading' control. It tests what a confident but wrong description costs. The model has no way to detect these errors, because it never sees a row.
